headline: Kansas governor’s veto stands, stopping proposed changes to education assessments
summary: The Kansas Senate failed to override Governor Laura Kelly’s vetoes of budget provisions that would have restructured state K-12 assessment tests and reset cut scores to address a reported 18% jump in proficiency rates, which Republicans argued was necessary for data continuity but Democrats decried as legislative overreach. Kelly also vetoed a plan to divert $8.25 million in existing education funds to teacher mentoring and professional development programs, and with the Senate falling short of the two-thirds majority needed to override, the State Board of Education retains authority over assessment standards while funding for those educator initiatives remains blocked.
